title: Olympic rings for SIZE + Iron Bull Strength Rings product review
summary: NH reviews the Iron Bull Strength wooden rings and explains how to use rings for hypertrophy. Bodybuilders only need the easy end of the rings' steep technical curve, not gymnast skills. He recommends wooden rings, cautious progressions for shoulders, elbows and biceps, AMRAP bodyweight work, high upper-body frequency, and inverted rows as the best ring exercise.
claims: Every lift has a technical grading: how much practice is needed before technique stops being the limiting factor
Curls have a low technical grading; front squats a high one; rings have the highest at full mastery
Bodybuilders only need the low end of ring skill; you do not need iron crosses or planches to grow
Gymnasts have big biceps because rings are their entire sport; reaching their level would mean sacrificing everything else, including legs
NH could do ring pull-ups and ring rows the first time he tried; anyone with a bodyweight background learns the basics fast
Buy wooden rings: metal and plastic ones are slippery, damage easily, rust and can cut you
The three indispensable pieces of home training equipment are a pull-up bar, rings and elastic bands
Rings only train the upper body: horizontal and vertical pulls and horizontal pushes; vertical presses require ring handstand push-ups
Rings work the biceps partly because rotating the arms while locked out in a press stretches the biceps, which also risks biceps injury
With any new equipment start easy; on an SSB bar do not load even 70% of your max squat at first
Start ring push-ups with feet on the floor and rings high, and ring rows with rings low enough to limit range
Rings let shoulders go deeper than the floor allows, so avoid fast negatives, lower slowly and increase depth over time
Rings are a great injury prevention tool because of the extra range of motion they allow beyond the bench press
Be careful with ring dips and ring triceps extensions; they tax elbows and shoulders
NH hurt his shoulder and elbow when starting rings by internally rotating his shoulders without paying attention
Progress ring dips from feet on the floor, to feet on a box, to feet off the floor with knees raised
Because rings move with your wrists, they suit people who have wrist pain on presses
Avoid a thumbless grip on wooden rings; it is slippery and pointless since rings already reduce shoulder stress
Do unweighted bodyweight movements like ring push-ups and ring rows for as many reps as possible; once loaded, AMRAP is less conducive to progression
Let legs rest two days after destroying them, but sneak ring sets into the upper body often to accumulate volume
Biceps fatigue fast but recover fast, and on rings they are a supporting muscle rather than the limiting factor
Inverted rows are the most underrated upper-back movement; changing grip and pull width lights up different parts of the upper back
The Iron Bull Strength rings cost about $30 and are worth it for rows alone; NH is not sponsored
exercises: start feet on floor, rings high; slow negatives
start rings low; vary chin-up, neutral, pronated grips and width
progress feet on floor, on box, then off floor; watch shoulder depth
chest/triceps; taxing on elbows and shoulders
easy to learn for those with bodyweight background
